summary: Escape Plan is a Vital Lacerda puzzle game where thief characters race across a modular hex city map to reach an exit before lockdown, picking up cash and dodging obstacles along asymmetric character powers. It's a tighter, shorter, more accessible design than Lacerda's usual heavy fare, playing almost like a movement puzzle race.
praised: Clever modular map and route-planning puzzle
Shorter and lighter than typical Lacerda games while retaining clever design
Strong player asymmetry via unique character powers
High production values and thematic heist framing
criticised: Can feel more solitaire/puzzly than interactive
Some find the theme thin compared to the mechanical puzzle
Less depth than Lacerda's flagship titles like Vinhos or On Mars
Niche appeal since it doesn't fit the 'usual heavy Lacerda' expectation

interaction.kind: race and area denial on a shared map
interaction.detail: All players move across the same modular city map, racing to grab money tiles and secure an escape route before rivals reach the same hexes first. Route and path tiles come from a shared pool that is drafted round by round, but no action targets an opponent directly.

scoring.how_you_win: Collect as much hidden money as possible while building a viable route out of the city, then successfully escape before it's locked down; most money (with bonuses) wins.
